records.title: Demand for Integrated Buckingham Canal–based multimodal corridor in Andhra Pradesh under NW-4 with key focus on SPS Nellore district.
details:
Shri Masthan Rao
Yadav Beeda: 
I draw attention of the Government to the
urgent need for integrated development of the Buckingham Canal corridor in
Andhra Pradesh, particularly in Sri Potti Sriramulu Nellore District, under
National Waterway-4 (NW-4). This calls for coordinated action by the Ministry
of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI),
and convergence with the Sagarmala and Bharatmala programmes. Buckingham Canal
traverses about 257?258 km in Andhra Pradesh, and the Nellore stretches are
less encroached and technically feasible. Official alignment studies and
KML-based mapping demarcate a 60-metre waterway corridor and a 30-metre
parallel road corridor, safeguarding canal boundaries while enabling planned
infrastructure development. This allows simultaneous canal restoration and road
development, unlike congested urban stretches elsewhere on NW-4.? The Nellore
corridor provides multimodal connectivity between Krishnapatnam Port and the
proposed Ramapatnam Port, linking industrial hubs and hinterland areas. A combined
road-and-waterway corridor can reduce logistics costs, decongest highways and
improve industrial efficiency. It also offers scope for five to six future
industrial cities, generating employment and balanced regional growth. The
Union Budget 2026?27 reiterates emphasis on inland waterways, port-led
development, multimodal logistics, and coastal infrastructure. The Buckingham
Canal corridor is a natural candidate for convergence. I urge the Government to
sanction a Detailed Project Report (DPR), take up the Nellore stretch as a
pilot corridor, and establish a Centre?State mechanism with IWAI for time-bound
execution.
(ENDS)

records.title: Need to Enhance Allocation under MPLADS.
details:
Shri Masthan Rao
Yadav Beeda: 
I seek to raise an important issue
concerning the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS),
which is a vital instrument for addressing local developmental needs. At
present, each Member of Parliament is allocated ₹5 crore per year under
MPLADS. However, the effective value of development works executed on the ground
is considerably reduced due to statutory deductions such as GST at 18%,
seigniorage charges of around 5%, quality control charges, and other mandatory
recoveries during implementation. As a result, the actual developmental output
comes down to nearly 75% of the sanctioned amount. Consequently, from the
nominal allocation of ₹5 crore, the real value of works executed is only
about ₹3.5 to ₹3.75 crore. This limits the ability of MPs to
adequately meet growing local demands relating to rural infrastructure, drinking
water, education, health facilities, and community assets. At the same time,
the cost of construction materials, labour, and infrastructure development has
increased substantially due to inflation and rising input prices. Despite these
changes, the MPLADS allocation has remained unchanged for several years, making
it increasingly difficult to undertake meaningful and impactful projects,
particularly in rural and backward areas. In view of these realities, I urge
the Government to consider enhancing the annual MPLADS allocation from ₹5
crore to at least ₹10 crore per Member of Parliament. Such an increase
will enable MPs to respond more effectively to constituency needs, strengthen
grassroots infrastructure, and ensure better developmental outcomes for the
people.
(ENDS)

records.title: Demand for disclosure and monitoring of OBC representation in senior management of Public Sector Banks.
details:
Shri Masthan Rao
Yadav Beeda:
???????????????????????????????????????????????????????????? 
I seek to raise the matter of
representation of Other Backward Classes (OBCs) in senior and leadership
positions in Public Sector Banks (PSBs), in the light of the Department of
Financial Services (DFS) Annual Report 2025?26. Public Sector Banks, as public
institutions, are expected to reflect the constitutional principles of
equality, inclusion and social justice at decision-making levels. The DFS
Annual Report 2025?26 states that from 01 April 2025, the sanctioned strength
of senior management cadres i.e., Assistant General Manager, Deputy
General Manager, General Manager and Chief General Manager, has been increased
to strengthen governance and operational efficiency.? However, the report does
not provide bank-wise or cadre-wise data on the social-category composition of
officers, particularly OBCs. Without such information, it is difficult to
assess whether the expansion of senior posts has ensured equitable
representation. Further, there is no consolidated data on promotions to
Scale-IV and above since 2021, including the number of officers belonging to
the OBC category. Similarly, appointments of Managing Directors, Chief
Executive Officers and Executive Directors are listed without indicating their
social-category profile. Therefore, I urge the Government to direct DFS, in
coordination with the Reserve Bank of India, the Ministry of Social Justice and
Empowerment and the National Commission for Backward Classes, to publish
bank-wise data on senior posts with social-category break-up, disclose
promotion statistics, ensure OBC representation in selection panels, and
strengthen reservation monitoring mechanisms in all PSBs.
(ENDS)

records.title: Concern over Quantum Valley and Quantum Teaching Labs.
details:
Shri Masthan Rao Yadav Beeda: I draw
attention of the Government to the need for supporting Andhra Pradesh?s Quantum
Valley initiative and for including the State in the national programme for
establishing Quantum Teaching Labs in engineering institutions. Quantum
technology is an emerging and strategic field with applications in computing,
communications, cybersecurity, healthcare, materials science and defence.?
Andhra Pradesh has taken proactive steps through the proposed Quantum Valley
initiative to build an ecosystem for advanced research, education and industry
collaboration. However, the success of this initiative depends on strong
support from the Union Government and its integration with national efforts
such as the National Quantum Mission. Establishing Quantum Teaching Labs in
engineering colleges across the State will help create a skilled workforce by
providing students with hands-on training and early exposure to quantum
concepts. These labs will strengthen research capacity, improve faculty skills
and bridge the gap between academic learning and advanced technologies.?
Inclusion of Andhra Pradesh in the national rollout will also ensure regional
balance and equal access to modern scientific infrastructure. I request the
Union Government to extend financial and institutional support to the Quantum
Valley initiative and include Andhra Pradesh under the national programme for
setting up Quantum Teaching Labs, so as to promote innovation, generate
high-skilled employment, and strengthen India?s leadership and self-reliance in
emerging technologies.
(ENDS)

records.title: Demand for operationalization of South Coast Railway (SCOR) Zone.
details:
Shri Masthan Rao Yadav Beeda: I bring to
notice of the Government the long-pending issue of operationalising the South
Coast Railway Zone with its headquarters at Visakhapatnam, as assured under the
Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation framework. The new railway zone was envisaged to
correct regional imbalances, improve administrative efficiency and accelerate
railway infrastructure development in Andhra Pradesh. Although some preliminary
steps have been taken, including the initiation of staff transfers from South
Central Railway, the South Coast Railway Zone is yet to become fully
functional. The absence of a formal gazette notification, independent budgetary
allocation and full administrative autonomy has delayed the expected benefits.
As a result, important decisions related to railway expansion, passenger
facilities, freight movement and project execution continue to face avoidable
procedural delays. Operationalising SCOR is crucial for improving rail
connectivity across coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema, enhancing freight
handling for ports and industrial corridors and strengthening passenger
services in fast-growing urban regions. A functional zone will also support
port-led development, industrial growth and employment generation, especially
in port cities and backward districts.I urge the Union Government to expedite
the issuance of the formal gazette notification, provide adequate budgetary
support, ensure full administrative and operational independence, and clearly
outline a time-bound roadmap for making the South Coast Railway Zone fully
operational. Timely action is essential to honour commitments made to the
people of Andhra Pradesh and to strengthen regional rail infrastructure in line
with national development goals.
(ENDS)

records.title: Regarding Project on the Nucleus Breeding Centre
details:
SHRI
MASTHAN RAO BEEDA: Madam, project on the Nucleus Breeding
Centre for Indian Tiger Shrimp was established more than a decade ago in
Andaman under the supervision of Marine Products Export Development Authority
(MPEDA). So far, no Specific Pathogen Free (SPF) brood stock has been made
available to the hatchery operators. It is necessary to supply indigenous brood
stock of Tiger Shrimp immediately by MPEDA to bring sustainability of
aquaculture in the country instead of depending on the imported brood stock.
It
is learnt that a foreign company has been permitted to establish Broodstock
Multiplication Centre (BMC) in India along with the Indian hatchery operator
causing monopolistic situation which is not desirable. 
I
urge the Government of India to direct MPEDA to expedite the arrangements for
supplying Black Tiger Brood Stock from its Andaman Project to the hatchery
operators. Thank you.
(Ends)
